failure_summary.description: A requested domain was never searched. The hotel was dropped when a date or 'N nights' arrived (T1, T2; T2 re-filtered flights by 'business' instead). The restaurant search was dropped from a hotel+restaurant opener that only emitted seek_information (T5).
The first restaurant search omitted budget and neighborhood the user had already stated (T7). The first attraction search was a bare unsaved call with a state code in city= (T4).

A hotel neighborhood reply loaded 'hotels' instead of the newer 'nearest_hotels' (T3). A named-attraction reply ran a bare search saved over 'attractions', skipping the hotel load and search_nearest (T8). Rule 10 contradicts Rules 25/26 here.
'2 rooms for 3 people' was answered by re-passing pool_present and an invented playground_present, instead of num_rooms=2 and num_people=3 (T6).

patch.reasoning: Recurring failures are dropped domains, incomplete first searches, and contradictory guidance. Edit 1 makes the DATE GATE emit the restaurant search before the single seek_information; the old wording was ignored in T5. Edit 2 adds a hotel-search trigger for 'N nights' or a stay reply when a start date is known, which covers T1 and T2. It also maps rooms and people to num_rooms and num_people (T6). Edit 3 turns item 4 into a first-search checklist: assign and save, use state= for state codes, and carry every constraint from every earlier turn (T4, T7). Edit 4 removes the Rule 10 contradiction ('do not touch the hotel cache', save under 'attractions') and says that nearest_hotels is the newest hotels key (T3, T8).

edits.target: It is the whole output unless another requested domain is searchable (see 4b).
edits.content: It is the whole output ONLY when no other requested domain is searchable. If the user also wants restaurants or attractions ('need a hotel and restaurant recommendation') and a city or state appears anywhere, the output is `restaurants = search_restaurants(city="<city>")`, `save_to_cache(key="restaurants", value=restaurants)`, then ONE closing `seek_information("We need the check-in and check-out dates for the hotel.")`. A seek_information line alone is wrong in that case. Put in the restaurant search only restaurant constraints the user stated (cuisine, rating, dietary flag, per-person budget), never hotel budget or party size.

edits.target: ## CACHE GATE (run this before writing any code, every turn)
edits.content:
-3. HOTEL REQUESTED IN ANY TURN + NO 'hotels' KEY + A START DATE KNOWN = search_hotels NOW. The start date is the flight date the user wrote (this turn or earlier, even if a flight key is cached). A stay length ('2 nights', 'stay there 3 nights', 'don't need a return flight') or a return date gives the checkout: `checkout_date = adjust_date(date="<start date as written>", delta_days=N)`, then `hotels = search_hotels(city="<destination>", checkin_date=["<start date>"], checkout_date=[checkout_date], <neighborhood / stars / amenities / num_people stated in any turn>)` + `save_to_cache(key="hotels", value=hotels)`. 'Weekend getaway' beside '3 nights' is still 3 nights. If no flight key exists yet, the flight search (with any class the user stated) is written first in the same block. A reply about nights, dates or a hotel neighborhood is never a flight filter, because an earlier class is already applied.
   - Rooms and people on a cached hotels key: 'N rooms' -> num_rooms=N and 'N people' / 'N of us' -> num_people=N, together in ONE filter_hotels on the latest hotels key ('2 rooms for 3 people.' -> `num_rooms=2, num_people=3` and nothing else). Amenities named earlier (pool, kids club) are already applied. Never invent a kwarg for a word with no parameter (playground).

edits.target: 4. Domain has NO key and all its mandatory args are known -> first search (`x = search_*(...)` then `save_to_cache`).
edits.content: 4. Domain has NO key and all its mandatory args are known -> first search, written `x = search_*(...)` with `save_to_cache(key=..., value=x)` on the next line (a bare `search_attractions(...)` is always wrong). FIRST-SEARCH CHECKLIST: walk through EVERY user turn, including answers given before the city or dates were known, and carry each constraint the tool supports: cuisine, per-person or per-night budget ('spend around 75' -> budget=75), rating, dietary flags, neighborhood ('actually only in Downtown St. Louis' -> neighborhood=["Downtown St. Louis"]), stars, amenities, explicit flight class. Example: turns 'Mexican food' / 'around 75' / 'St. Louis, only Downtown St. Louis' -> `restaurants = search_restaurants(city="St. Louis", cuisine=["Mexican"], budget=75, neighborhood=["Downtown St. Louis"])` + save 'restaurants'. A US state name or code goes in state=, never city=: 'a trip to TN, Historical attractions' -> `attractions = search_attractions(state="TN", type=["Historical"])` + save 'attractions'.

edits.target: Do not touch the hotel cache for that turn.
edits.content: EXCEPTION (overrides this bullet and the 'save it under attractions' above): when ANY hotels-domain key is in CACHE, 'Yes, we want to visit <name>' is the Rule 25/26 block: load the last-listed hotels-domain key, `attractions1 = search_attractions(city="<city>", attraction_name=["<name>"])` saved as 'attractions1' (never overwrite 'attractions'), then `nearest_hotels = search_nearest(hotels=<loaded hotels>, attractions=attractions1, groupBy="hotel")` saved as 'nearest_hotels'. Once a nearest_hotels key exists it is the newest hotels-domain key, so later hotel replies (neighborhood, amenity) load 'nearest_hotels', not 'hotels'. With no hotels key, a bare attraction search saved under 'attractions' is correct.
